prompt: I run a Shopify store and I'm losing sales every time something sells out — shoppers see "Sold out" and leave without telling me they were interested. I want a "Notify me when back in stock" app so any shopper can leave their email on a sold-out item and hear from me the moment it's available again, and I can see in the admin which products people are waiting on so I know what to restock. Shoppers should sign up at the variant level when a product has multiple variants like sizes or colors (they pick the exact one and only get notified about that one), or at the product level when there's nothing meaningful to choose between — default to whichever fits. The widget sits on the product page right under the sold-out button, takes an email, confirms inline, and never appears on items already in stock. When something is back, every shopper waiting should be emailed in the order they signed up; if only a few units come back and many are waiting, notify the front of the queue and keep the rest for the next restock, and each shopper hears about a given item once per restock so no duplicate blasts if stock briefly dips. In the admin I want a dashboard ranking products by waitlist size, a drill-in to see individual subscribers and export them as CSV, an editor for the email subject and body (with product name, item details, and a one-click unsubscribe link), and quiet hours so nothing sends late at night. Every email needs a working unsubscribe that clears the shopper from all their waitlists; deleted products clear their waitlist cleanly; duplicate signups for the same item from the same email are a no-op; the same email across many products is fine. The number I care about most is "lost demand recovered" — how many signed up, how many got notified, and how many of those actually bought that item within a week.

intent.desiredOutcome: Recover lost sales by capturing shopper interest in sold-out items, notifying them intelligently when stock returns, and showing the merchant demand-recovery metrics.
intent.cronHint: every 1 hour (inventory polling) + on-demand restock detection
intent.qualityBrief: A mature back-in-stock notifier handles duplicate signups (same email + variant = no-op), respects quiet hours by deferring sends until the window opens, tracks per-shopper-per-product notification state so no duplicate blasts if stock briefly dips, and cleanly removes waitlist entries when products are deleted. The widget must appear only on actually sold-out variants (not low-stock), default to variant-level signup when variants exist, and show inline confirmation with an option to manage subscriptions. The admin dashboard ranks products by waitlist urgency, shows export-ready lists, and includes a customizable email template with one-click unsubscribe links. Conversion metrics ("did this shopper buy within a week?") require linking the notified email to Shopify orders, with a fallback for guest checkout.

plan.dataFlow: When a shopper lands on a sold-out product page, the widget calls the availability-check endpoint (live Storefront API query) and, if truly out-of-stock, renders the signup form; on submission the backend inserts a waitlist entry (deduping on email + item key). When an inventory-level update webhook fires, the backend resolves the inventory item to a variant, compares the new quantity against the last-known snapshot to detect a zero-crossing, and — if one is found — creates a restock_event; the hourly dispatch job then picks up pending restock events, selects the front of the waiting queue up to the configured notify-quota, creates a notification_batch, creates notification_record rows for each addressee, and emails them (respecting quiet hours by deferring to the next open window). When an order is paid, the backend inspects line items and for any variant whose email appears in recently-notified notification_records within the attribution window, a conversion_event row is inserted. The merchant sees the admin dashboard (waitlist rankings, drill-in, email template editor, quiet-hours config) at all times, with CSV export available per item.

triggers.event: an inventory level is updated at a location
triggers.idempotency: if a restock_event already exists for this inventory item at this inventory_level_updated_at timestamp, treat the event as a no-op

triggers.event: a product is deleted from the store
triggers.idempotency: if the product's waitlist entries are already removed, treat the event as a no-op

triggers.event: an order is paid by a customer
triggers.idempotency: if a conversion_event already exists for this order identifier, treat the event as a no-op

triggers.jobPurpose: Dispatch back-in-stock notification emails for pending restock events, respecting quiet hours and per-restock notify quotas.
triggers.perTickWork: For each pending restock_event not yet fully dispatched, select waitlist entries at the front of the queue up to the configured notify-quota that have not already been notified for this restock event, create a notification_batch, enqueue one notification_record per recipient, send emails, and mark the batch dispatched.

capabilities.description: Query Shopify Storefront API in real time to determine whether a specific variant or product is currently out of stock, so the widget only renders the signup form on genuinely sold-out items.

shopifySteps.produces: availableForSale flag per variant and for the product

capabilities.description: Insert a new waitlist entry for a shopper's email on a specific out-of-stock item, ignoring duplicate signups for the same email and item.
Look up the variant and product identifiers from a Shopify inventory item id so an inventory update can be matched to the correct waitlist entries.

shopifySteps.produces: variant external id and product external id via variant field

capabilities.description: Compare incoming inventory available quantity against the last-known snapshot to detect a zero-crossing and create a restock event when an item transitions from out-of-stock to available.
Retrieve product title and variant display name from Shopify to populate the notification email template at send time.

shopifySteps.produces: variant title, display name, product title, and product URL

capabilities.description: Select the front of the waitlist queue up to the configured notify quota, create a notification batch and individual records, and schedule send respecting quiet hours.
Send a single back-in-stock notification email to one subscriber with the merchant's configured subject template, product details, and an embedded unsubscribe link.
Update a notification record's status to sent or failed and record the send timestamp.
Deactivate all active waitlist entries for a shopper identified by their unsubscribe token, processing a one-click unsubscribe from a notification email.
Remove all waitlist entries and mark related availability snapshots stale for a product when it is deleted from the store.
On a paid order, match buyer email and purchased variant item keys against recently-notified notification records within the configured attribution window and record a conversion event.
Return products and variants ranked by active waitlist size for the merchant admin dashboard.
Return a paginated list of individual subscriber entries for a specific item for the merchant drill-in view.
Produce a CSV of all subscriber entries for a specific item for the merchant to download.
Return the current app settings for the merchant admin settings page.
Persist updated quiet hours, notify quota, and conversion attribution window from the merchant admin settings form.
Return aggregate counts of signups, notifications sent, and confirmed conversions per item for the admin metrics view.

persistence.name: waitlist_entries
persistence.purpose: Stores each shopper's signup for a specific out-of-stock item, keyed to prevent duplicate registrations.

columns.name: email
columns.purpose: shopper email address to notify

columns.name: item_key
columns.purpose: natural key for the item being waited on: variant external id when item_type is variant, product external id when item_type is product

columns.name: item_type
columns.purpose: either variant or product, distinguishes how item_key should be resolved to a Shopify resource

columns.name: product_external_id
columns.purpose: product identifier used for grouping on dashboard and bulk cleanup on product deletion

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: variant identifier; null when item_type is product

columns.name: unsubscribe_token
columns.purpose: unique opaque token embedded in notification email links for one-click unsubscribe

columns.name: is_active
columns.purpose: false after shopper unsubscribes or entry is purged on product deletion

columns.name: signed_up_at
columns.purpose: used to order the notification queue FIFO per restock event

queryPatterns: active entries for a given item_key ordered by signed_up_at ascending (notification queue)
all entries for a given product_external_id (product deletion cleanup)
all active entries for a given email (bulk unsubscribe)
count of active entries per item_key ordered descending (dashboard ranking)
paginated entries for a given item_key (drill-in and export)

persistence.name: restock_events
persistence.purpose: Records each detected zero-crossing from out-of-stock to available for an item, driving the notification dispatch queue.

columns.name: item_key
columns.purpose: item that became available, matches waitlist_entries.item_key

columns.name: inventory_item_external_id
columns.purpose: Shopify inventory item id from the webhook, part of the dedup key

columns.name: inventory_level_updated_at
columns.purpose: value of updated_at bound from the inventory_levels/update webhook payload; used as the dedup key partner so two re-deliveries of the same webhook event carry the same timestamp and the unique constraint on (inventory_item_external_id, inventory_level_updated_at) prevents a duplicate restock_event row

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: lifecycle: pending (awaiting dispatch), dispatching (job in progress), completed (all eligible subscribers notified for this event)

queryPatterns: pending or dispatching restock events ordered by created_at (hourly job pickup)
single lookup by inventory_item_external_id to compare against snapshot for zero-crossing detection

persistence.name: notification_batches
persistence.purpose: Groups a set of notification sends for a single restock event dispatch run, enabling quota tracking, quiet-hours deferral, and status auditing.

columns.name: restock_event_id
columns.purpose: the restock event this batch serves

columns.name: item_key
columns.purpose: item being notified about, denormalized for query convenience

columns.name: scheduled_send_at
columns.purpose: earliest time emails may be sent; pushed past quiet_hours_end when the batch is created inside a quiet window

columns.name: sent_count
columns.purpose: number of emails actually sent in this batch

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: lifecycle: pending, sending, sent, failed

queryPatterns: pending batches whose scheduled_send_at is now or in the past (dispatch job)

persistence.name: notification_records
persistence.purpose: One row per shopper per restock event notified; prevents duplicate blasts when stock briefly dips and re-triggers.

columns.name: restock_event_id
columns.purpose: direct reference for dedup queries without joining through batch

columns.name: email
columns.purpose: denormalized for conversion matching and audit

columns.name: item_key
columns.purpose: denormalized for conversion matching

columns.name: status
columns.purpose: lifecycle: queued, sent, failed

columns.name: sent_at
columns.purpose: null until email is confirmed sent; used in conversion attribution window query

queryPatterns: exists check by waitlist_entry_id + restock_event_id (duplicate blast prevention)
records by email + item_key with sent_at within conversion window (conversion matching)

persistence.name: conversion_events
persistence.purpose: Records when a notified shopper purchases the item they were waiting for within the conversion attribution window.

columns.name: notification_record_id
columns.purpose: the specific notification that preceded this purchase

columns.name: order_external_id
columns.purpose: the paid order that triggered conversion detection

columns.name: email
columns.purpose: buyer email as supplied by the order; may differ from waitlist email for guest checkouts

queryPatterns: exists check by order_external_id + item_key (dedup on duplicate order paid delivery)
conversion rate per item: notification_records count vs conversion_events count

persistence.name: item_availability_snapshots
persistence.purpose: Tracks the last-known available quantity for each inventory item so the system can detect a true zero-crossing rather than reacting to every inventory update.

columns.name: inventory_item_external_id
columns.purpose: Shopify inventory item identifier from the webhook

columns.name: variant_external_id
columns.purpose: resolved via inventoryItem GraphQL query; null until first resolution succeeds

columns.name: item_key
columns.purpose: resolved item_key matching waitlist_entries.item_key; null until variant resolution succeeds

columns.name: last_available_qty
columns.purpose: available quantity from the most recent inventory_levels/update; null before first update

columns.name: availability_status
columns.purpose: last-observed state: unknown, out_of_stock, or in_stock

columns.name: updated_at
columns.purpose: timestamp of the last processed inventory_levels/update webhook

queryPatterns: upsert by inventory_item_external_id on every inventory_levels/update to detect zero-crossing
lookup by item_key to cross-check live availability for widget

persistence.name: app_settings
persistence.purpose: Single-row merchant configuration for quiet hours, notify quota, and conversion attribution window.

columns.name: id
columns.purpose: singleton row; application code ensures exactly one row exists

columns.name: quiet_hours_start
columns.purpose: hour of day 0-23 when the quiet window begins; emails are deferred if the current hour is within the window

columns.name: quiet_hours_end
columns.purpose: hour of day 0-23 when the quiet window ends; deferred batches resume at this hour

columns.name: notify_quota
columns.purpose: maximum subscribers to notify per restock event dispatch run; remainder waits for the next restock

columns.name: conversion_window_days
columns.purpose: number of days after a notification is sent within which a purchase counts as a conversion

columns.name: email_subject_template
columns.purpose: merchant-configured email subject line template, may include placeholders for product name and item details

queryPatterns: single row fetch on every dispatch job run and every conversion detection

transitions.trigger: first inventory update received with available quantity at zero or below
first inventory update received with available quantity above zero
inventory update shows available quantity crossing above zero — triggers a restock event
inventory update shows available quantity dropping to zero or below

invariants: A restock event is created only on the out_of_stock → in_stock transition, never on any other transition
The item_availability_snapshots row for an inventory item is the sole source of truth for the last-known availability status
Widget availability checks always call the Storefront API live and never rely solely on the snapshot

Add a shopper's email to the waitlist for a specific out-of-stock item.

Return a paginated list of products/variants ranked by waitlist size for the merchant overview.
Return a paginated list of individual subscriber entries for a specific item so the merchant can drill in.
Export all subscriber entries for a specific item as a CSV file download.
Return the current app settings including email subject template, quiet hours window, and notify quota.
Save updated app settings for email subject template, quiet hours, and notify quota.
Return demand-recovery metrics: total signups, total notified, and confirmed conversions per item.

edgeCases: Duplicate inventory_levels/update delivery for the same inventory item and timestamp — the system detects the existing snapshot row with identical updated_at and exits without creating a duplicate restock_event.

Inventory briefly dips back to zero and then returns while a notification batch is still pending — the second restock event is created normally, but notification_records keyed on waitlist_entry_id + restock_event_id prevent the same subscriber from receiving two emails for the same restock cycle.

A restock event fires during the quiet hours window — the dispatch job creates the notification_batch with scheduled_send_at deferred to the end of the quiet window, and the hourly job skips it until that time has passed.

A product is deleted while a notification batch is mid-dispatch — purge-product-waitlist marks entries inactive; any in-flight sends for already-queued notification_records complete, but newly selected entries are skipped because their waitlist_entry is no longer active.

A shopper places an order as a guest with a different email than their waitlist entry — conversion detection matches on order email against notification_records.email; no match means no conversion recorded, which is a known gap documented as a guest-checkout limitation.

Duplicate orders/paid delivery for the same order — the conversion_events unique key on order_external_id + item_key ensures at-most-one conversion row per item per order regardless of webhook re-delivery.

hld_v_findings.issue: The `app_settings` table declares columns `[id, quiet_hours_start, quiet_hours_end, notify_quota, conversion_window_days]` — there is no `email_subject_template` or `email_body_template` column. Yet `POST /admin/settings` requestShape includes `"email_subject_template": "text"`, and the `send-restock-email` capability lists `"email subject template"` as a dataNeed. The admin contract writes a setting that has no backing column; the notify capability consumes a value that nothing stores. This is phantom storage: the coding agent will either fabricate a column name or silently drop the template feature.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add `email_subject_template` (role: text, nullable: false) and `email_body_template` (role: text, nullable: false) columns to `app_settings`, and add `email_body_template` to the `POST /admin/settings` requestShape.

hld_v_findings.issue: The `restock_events` dedup key is `["inventory_item_external_id", "detected_at"]`, and the column's purpose states it holds "the timestamp of the inventory_levels/update webhook." However, the `inventory_levels/update` payloadBindings bind only `inventory_item_id`, `available`, and `location_id` — no timestamp field is bound from the payload. If `detected_at` is set to `NOW()` at insertion time, two re-deliveries of the same webhook will each get a different wall-clock value and the dedup key will not fire. The coding agent has no declared source for the timestamp value that the dedup actually depends on.
hld_v_findings.fix: Add a `signalField` of "inventory level updated at" to the `inventory_levels/update` trigger with a payloadBinding to `payloadPath: "updated_at"` (present on the payload), rename the `restock_events` column accordingly, and use that bound value — not `NOW()` — as the dedup timestamp.

hld_v_findings.issue: The spec states `statusField` is "RESERVED for binding a column to a non-null stateMachine." The only declared `stateMachine` in the plan is bound to `item_availability_snapshots.availability_status`. Yet `restock_events`, `notification_batches`, and `notification_records` all declare a non-null `statusField: "status"` with no corresponding stateMachine. These are internal application workflow lifecycles (correctly excluded from a stateMachine per spec), so their `statusField` should be `null`; the `usesWorkflow` flag on the owning capabilities already binds the workflow helper for those columns.
hld_v_findings.fix: Set `statusField: null` on `restock_events`, `notification_batches`, and `notification_records`; the `usesWorkflow: true` flags on `detect-restock`, `dispatch-notification-batch`, and `record-notification-outcome` are the correct and sufficient binding for the workflow helper.
